baslik: One Design Change Doubled the Load — and 114 Died
sonuc: collapsed onto a crowded hotel lobby
tetik: a rod change that doubled the load on one connection
mekanizma: box-beam connection pull-through from a doubled hanger-rod load
ders: connection changes during fabrication now need the engineer of record's approval
zincir: LOAD ON UPPER BOX BEAM DOUBLES

zaman.olay: Tea dance in the atrium; walkways crowded

yanilgi: The original design was already weak. The fabrication change made it far worse: one hanger connection had to carry two walkways.
tartisma: The change was approved without a new calculation. Who owns a connection — the designer or the fabricator?
basliklar: One Design Change Doubled the Load — and 114 Died
Why the Hyatt Regency Walkways Fell
The Rod Change That Collapsed a Hotel
sahneler: Two walkways fell onto a crowded hotel lobby in Kansas City.
In seconds, one hundred fourteen people were dead.
So how does a walkway just drop?
The design used one long rod through both walkways.
During construction, it was swapped for two shorter rods.
That quietly doubled the load on one set of nuts.
Under the crowd, the nuts pulled straight through the beam.
Now every connection change needs the engineer's approval.

kaynakca.ad: NBS Building Science Series 143 — Investigation of the Kansas City Hyatt Regency Walkways Collapse

baslik: A Crack Smaller Than a Coin Dropped a Whole Bridge
sonuc: fell into the Ohio River at rush hour
tetik: a tiny crack in one eyebar
mekanizma: stress corrosion cracking in an eyebar of a non-redundant chain
ders: US bridges now get mandatory inspections under the National Bridge Inspection Standards

zaman.olay: Rush-hour traffic on the bridge

yanilgi: It wasn't overloaded by one heavy truck. The bridge hung on eyebar chains with no redundancy, so one cracked link was enough.
tartisma: The crack was hidden inside a joint no inspector could see. Should designs without redundancy be allowed at all?
basliklar: A Crack Smaller Than a Coin Dropped a Whole Bridge
Why the Silver Bridge Collapsed
The Single Link That Killed 46 People
soru: Could you have seen the crack?
sahneler: At rush hour, an entire bridge fell into the Ohio River.
It collapsed in under a minute, and forty six people died.
The cause was a crack you could barely see.
It hid inside one eyebar in the suspension chain.
Corrosion and stress slowly grew it deeper.
When that single link snapped, nothing else could hold the load.
The bridge had no backup path.
That's why American bridges now get mandatory inspections.

kaynakca.ad: NTSB Highway Accident Report HAR-71-01 — Collapse of U.S. 35 Highway Bridge, Point Pleasant

baslik: The Undersized Steel Plate That Dropped a Freeway
sonuc: dropped into the Mississippi River during rush hour
tetik: gusset plates designed half as thick as needed
mekanizma: undersized gusset plates failing under added dead load and construction materials
ders: gusset plates are now checked in load ratings of truss bridges

zaman.olay: Evening rush hour; resurfacing work on the deck

yanilgi: Corrosion and fatigue were suspected first. Investigators found a design error: key gusset plates were only half the thickness they needed.
tartisma: The error sat in the drawings for forty years. How many other bridges carry a mistake nobody rechecks?
basliklar: The Undersized Steel Plate That Dropped a Freeway
Why the I-35W Bridge Collapsed
A 40-Year-Old Design Error, Then 13 Dead
sahneler: During rush hour, a freeway bridge fell into the Mississippi River.
Cars plunged with it, and thirteen people were killed.
The cause had been in the drawings for forty years.
Steel gusset plates were designed only half as thick as needed.
Over time, extra concrete added weight to the deck.
That day, construction materials were parked right above a weak plate.
The plate buckled, and the main span fell.
Now gusset plates are checked in every truss bridge rating.

kaynakca.ad: NTSB Highway Accident Report HAR-08-03 — Collapse of I-35W Highway Bridge

baslik: The Safety Test That Blew Up a Reactor
sonuc: exploded during a safety test
tetik: control rods with graphite tips that first increased power
mekanizma: positive void coefficient plus graphite-tipped control rods causing a power surge
ders: RBMK reactors were modified so control rods can no longer spike power

zaman.olay: Turbine rundown safety test; emergency shutdown pressed

yanilgi: Operators made mistakes, but the reactor design itself made the shutdown button increase power in its first seconds.
tartisma: The flaw was known to some designers before 1986. Was this operator error or design error?
basliklar: The Safety Test That Blew Up a Reactor
Why Chernobyl's Off Switch Made It Worse
How Pressing Shutdown Destroyed Reactor 4
hook: The off switch made it worse
sahneler: Reactor four at Chernobyl exploded during a safety test.
Within seconds, power surged and a steam blast tore off the roof.
The strangest part is what triggered it.
Operators pressed the emergency shutdown button.
But the control rods had graphite tips.
Entering the core, those tips first pushed power up, not down.
In an unstable reactor, that spike was enough.
These reactors were later changed so shutdown can never add power.

kaynakca.ad: IAEA INSAG-7 — The Chernobyl Accident: Updating of INSAG-1
US NRC — Backgrounder on Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant Accident

baslik: A Stuck Valve and a Misleading Light Melted a Reactor
sonuc: partially melted down
tetik: a relief valve stuck open while its light said closed
mekanizma: loss of coolant through a stuck-open pilot-operated relief valve, misread by operators
ders: control rooms were redesigned and operator training was overhauled

zaman.olay: Pumps trip; relief valve sticks open

yanilgi: The indicator light didn't lie about the valve — it showed only that the close signal was sent, not where the valve actually was.
tartisma: The operators followed their training. Was the failure human, or the control room design?
basliklar: A Stuck Valve and a Misleading Light Melted a Reactor
Why Three Mile Island Melted Down
The Light That Said Closed
sahneler: Part of the core at Three Mile Island melted down.
Cooling water escaped for hours through a valve stuck open.
The operators didn't know.
Their panel light said the valve was closed.
It only showed the close signal was sent, not the valve's position.
Thinking there was too much water, they cut emergency cooling.
The core overheated and partly melted.
That's why control rooms and training were rebuilt afterward.

kaynakca.ad: US NRC — Backgrounder on the Three Mile Island Accident

baslik: A Piece of Foam Destroyed Space Shuttle Columbia
sonuc: broke apart during re-entry
tetik: a suitcase-sized piece of foam hitting the left wing at launch
mekanizma: foam strike breaching a reinforced carbon-carbon panel on the wing's leading edge
ders: shuttles were inspected in orbit for heat-shield damage on every later flight
zincir: HOT GAS ENTERS WING ON RE-ENTRY

zaman.olay: Launch; foam strike on the left wing
Break-up during re-entry over Texas

yanilgi: Foam had hit shuttles on earlier flights, so it came to be treated as routine. That normalization is why the damage was never checked in orbit.
tartisma: Engineers asked for satellite images of the wing and were turned down. What should happen when a warning is inconvenient?
basliklar: A Piece of Foam Destroyed Space Shuttle Columbia
Why Columbia Broke Apart on Re-entry
The Foam Strike Nobody Checked
soru: Would you have checked the wing?
sahneler: Space Shuttle Columbia broke apart as it came home.
All seven astronauts were killed minutes before landing.
The damage happened sixteen days earlier, at launch.
A piece of insulating foam hit the left wing.
It punched a hole in the heat shield panel.
On re-entry, superheated gas poured into the wing.
The structure melted from the inside.
After that, every shuttle's heat shield was inspected in orbit.

kaynakca.ad: NASA History Office — Columbia Accident Investigation Board Report

baslik: A Units Mix-Up Crashed a Mars Spacecraft
sonuc: was lost at Mars
tetik: ground software reporting thrust in pound-force seconds instead of newton-seconds
mekanizma: imperial-to-metric units mismatch in trajectory software
ders: interface specifications now state units explicitly and are verified end to end

zaman.olay: Orbit insertion; contact lost

yanilgi: It wasn't one big miscalculation. Tiny unit errors in many small thruster firings added up over the months-long cruise.
tartisma: Navigators noticed the trajectory drifting but the concern never escalated. How loud should a small anomaly be?
basliklar: A Units Mix-Up Crashed a Mars Spacecraft
Why Mars Climate Orbiter Was Lost
Pounds vs. Newtons: The Error That Ended a Mission
sahneler: A spacecraft reached Mars and vanished.
It dove too deep into the atmosphere and was destroyed.
The cause was a units mismatch.
One team's software reported thrust in pound-force seconds.
The navigation software expected newton-seconds.
Each small error pushed the spacecraft slightly off course.
Over months, they added up to a fatal miss.
Now interfaces must state their units and be checked end to end.

kaynakca.ad: NASA — Mars Climate Orbiter Mishap Investigation Board Phase I Report

baslik: One Line of Reused Code Blew Up Ariane 5
sonuc: self-destructed about 37 seconds after launch
tetik: a 64-bit number squeezed into a 16-bit integer
mekanizma: unprotected floating-point to integer conversion overflow in reused Ariane 4 software
ders: reused software is now re-verified against the new vehicle's real flight profile

zaman.olay: Maiden flight; overflow and self-destruct

yanilgi: The backup computer didn't save it because it ran the same code and failed the same way, just milliseconds earlier.
tartisma: The code had worked perfectly on Ariane 4. When is proven code not proven?
basliklar: One Line of Reused Code Blew Up Ariane 5
Why Ariane 5 Destroyed Itself
The Number Too Big for 16 Bits
sahneler: A brand new rocket destroyed itself about thirty seven seconds after launch.
It veered sideways, began breaking up and then exploded.
The cause was one number.
Guidance code copied from Ariane 4 squeezed a value into sixteen bits.
Ariane 5 flew faster, so the value got too big to fit.
The conversion overflowed, and both guidance computers shut down.
The backup failed because it ran the same code.
Reused software is now retested against the new rocket's real flight.

kaynakca.ad: ESA — Ariane 501 Inquiry Board report (press release)

baslik: The Roof Ripped Off a Plane at 24,000 Feet
sonuc: lost a large section of its roof in flight
tetik: tiny fatigue cracks linking up along a lap joint
mekanizma: multiple-site fatigue damage and corrosion in a fuselage lap joint
ders: ageing aircraft now get mandatory inspections for multiple-site fatigue damage
zincir: HUMID SALTY AIR, MANY SHORT FLIGHTS

zaman.olay: Explosive decompression near 24,000 ft

yanilgi: No single big crack did it. Many tiny cracks along a row of rivets joined into one long tear.
tartisma: A passenger reportedly saw a crack while boarding. How should a warning from a passenger be handled?
basliklar: The Roof Ripped Off a Plane at 24,000 Feet
How Aloha 243 Landed Without a Roof
The Tiny Cracks That Opened a Jet
sahneler: At twenty four thousand feet, the roof of a jet tore away.
The cabin tore open, and a flight attendant was killed.
So what ripped open a plane?
This jet had flown many short, salty island flights.
Corrosion loosened a joint along a row of rivets.
Tiny fatigue cracks grew, then linked into one long tear.
The pilots still landed it safely on Maui.
Now ageing aircraft are inspected for exactly this damage.

kaynakca.ad: NTSB Aircraft Accident Report AAR-89-03 — Aloha Airlines Flight 243

baslik: They Steered a Jet With Only the Engines
sonuc: lost all flight controls
tetik: a hidden flaw in a titanium fan disk
mekanizma: fatigue crack from a manufacturing defect shattering the tail engine's fan disk and severing all three hydraulic systems
ders: engine disks now get stricter inspections and hydraulic lines got fuses

zaman.olay: Tail engine fan disk fails in cruise

yanilgi: The jet had three separate hydraulic systems. Their lines ran close together in the tail, so one burst of debris cut them all.
tartisma: Redundancy failed because the backups shared one location. When is a backup not really a backup?
basliklar: They Steered a Jet With Only the Engines
How United 232 Lost All Three Hydraulic Systems
The Crack That Took Away Every Control
soru: Could you fly with only throttles?
sahneler: Mid-flight, a jet lost every flight control at once.
The tail engine exploded, and debris cut all three hydraulic systems.
The crew steered using only the engine throttles.
The cause was a hidden flaw inside a titanium fan disk.
A crack grew from it for years.
The backups failed because their lines ran side by side.
The crash landing still left most people alive.
Engine disks are now inspected far more strictly.

kaynakca.ad: NTSB Aircraft Accident Report AAR-90-06 — United Airlines Flight 232

baslik: Iced Sensors and a Stall Nobody Recognized
sonuc: fell into the Atlantic in a stall
tetik: ice crystals blocking the airspeed sensors
mekanizma: pitot tube icing causing autopilot disconnect, followed by a sustained aerodynamic stall
ders: pitot probes were replaced and crews now train on high-altitude stall recovery

zaman.olay: Pitot icing over the Atlantic; stall

yanilgi: The plane itself was flyable. The airspeed readings came back within about a minute, but the stall had already set in.
tartisma: The stall warning went quiet at very low airspeed, then sounded again when the nose lowered. How should a warning behave when data is unreliable?
basliklar: Iced Sensors and a Stall Nobody Recognized
Why Air France 447 Fell From the Sky
The Stall That Lasted Minutes
soru: Would you push the nose down?
sahneler: An airliner fell into the Atlantic Ocean.
It dropped for minutes in a deep stall, and all two hundred twenty eight aboard died.
It began with ice crystals.
They blocked the tubes that measure airspeed.
The autopilot disconnected, and the crew lost trusted speed data.
The nose was held up, and the wings stopped producing lift.
The stall was never recognized.
Now crews train for high-altitude stalls, and the sensors were replaced.

baslik: One Row of Rivets Instead of Two — 520 Died
sonuc: crashed into a mountain after losing its tail fin
tetik: a faulty repair with one row of rivets where two were needed
mekanizma: fatigue failure of an improperly repaired aft pressure bulkhead
ders: structural repairs are now inspected against the approved repair design
zincir: REPAIR USES ONE ROW OF RIVETS

zaman.olay: Bulkhead failure; crash on Mount Takamagahara

yanilgi: The accident began seven years earlier, with a repair after a tail strike on landing.
tartisma: The repair looked fine from outside. How do you inspect what a repair crew got wrong inside?
basliklar: One Row of Rivets Instead of Two — 520 Died
Why Japan Air Lines Flight 123 Lost Its Tail
The Repair That Failed Seven Years Later
sahneler: A jumbo jet's tail fin blew off in flight.
Thirty two minutes later, it crashed into a mountain, and five hundred twenty people died.
The failure started seven years earlier.
After a tail strike, a pressure bulkhead was repaired.
The repair used one row of rivets where two were needed.
Fatigue cracks grew until the bulkhead burst.
Escaping air tore off the fin and cut the hydraulics.
Repairs are now checked against their approved design.

kaynakca.ad: FAA Lessons Learned — Japan Airlines Flight 123, Boeing 747-SR100, JA8119

baslik: The First Jetliner Kept Breaking Apart in the Sky
sonuc: broke apart in flight
tetik: fatigue cracks at a corner of a cut-out in the cabin roof
mekanizma: metal fatigue from repeated pressurisation concentrated at sharp cut-out corners
ders: fuselages are now fatigue-tested in water tanks and designed to stop cracks

zaman.olay: BOAC Flight 781 breaks up near Elba

yanilgi: It wasn't a bomb or engine fire. Investigators proved it by pressurising a whole Comet in a water tank until the cabin cracked.
tartisma: The Comet was the world's first jet airliner. Can a first design ever be fully safe?
basliklar: The First Jetliner Kept Breaking Apart in the Sky
Why the de Havilland Comet Failed
The Water Tank Test That Solved the Comet Crashes
sahneler: The world's first jet airliner broke apart over the sea.
All thirty five people aboard died.
Then another Comet fell from the sky months later.
Investigators pressurized a whole Comet in a water tank, again and again.
The cabin split open at a sharp corner in the roof.
Every flight had stretched the metal, until fatigue cracked it.
Sharp corners concentrated the stress.
Since then, jets have rounded windows and fatigue-tested fuselages.

baslik: How Cladding Turned a Kitchen Fire Into a Tower Fire
sonuc: was engulfed by fire from top to bottom
tetik: a fridge-freezer fire reaching the outside of the building
mekanizma: polyethylene-core aluminium composite cladding and cavity insulation spreading fire up the facade
ders: combustible cladding was banned on tall residential buildings in England

zaman.olay: Kitchen fire on the fourth floor spreads up the facade

yanilgi: The fire didn't spread through the building's interior first. It climbed the outside, through the cladding, and entered flats from there.
tartisma: Residents were told to stay in their flats. When should a fire strategy be abandoned?
basliklar: How Cladding Turned a Kitchen Fire Into a Tower Fire
Why Grenfell Tower Burned So Fast
The Facade That Carried the Fire
sahneler: Fire raced up the outside of a London tower block.
Within about half an hour it reached the roof, and seventy two people died.
It began with a fridge-freezer in one flat.
Flames escaped through the window into the building's cladding.
Its panels had a plastic core that burned like fuel.
Fire climbed the facade and entered flats from outside.
Residents had been told to stay put.
England then banned combustible cladding on tall homes.

baslik: The Dam Survived — the Valley Didn't
sonuc: sent a giant wave over its crest
tetik: a mountainside sliding into the reservoir
mekanizma: a massive landslide displacing reservoir water over the dam
ders: reservoir slopes are now studied as closely as the dam itself

zaman.olay: Landslide into the reservoir; wave overtops the dam

yanilgi: The dam didn't break. It was the mountainside next to it that failed, and the dam survived almost intact.
tartisma: Warnings about the slope existed before the reservoir was filled. Who should have stopped it?
basliklar: The Dam Survived — the Valley Didn't
Why the Vajont Dam Disaster Happened
The Mountain That Fell Into a Lake
soru: Would you have filled the lake?
sahneler: A mountainside collapsed into a reservoir in the Italian Alps.
A giant wave rushed over the dam and destroyed the towns below.
Here's the strange part: the dam itself survived.
The failure was the slope beside the lake.
Filling the reservoir soaked and weakened that rock.
For years it crept, until it slid all at once.
The dam only guided the wave into the valley.
Now reservoir slopes are studied as closely as dams.

kaynakca.ad: ASDSO Dam Failures and Lessons Learned — Vajont Dam (Italy, 1963)

baslik: The Dam That Failed Hours After Being Declared Safe
sonuc: burst just before midnight
tetik: weak rock foundations softened by the reservoir
mekanizma: foundation failure of the dam's abutment rock, with uplift pressure under the dam
ders: California created state dam-safety oversight

zaman.olay: Inspection in the morning; failure just before midnight

yanilgi: The leak seen that morning looked like normal seepage. The real weakness was the rock the dam stood on.
tartisma: The chief engineer inspected it the same day and called it safe. What would you have needed to see?
basliklar: The Dam That Failed Hours After Being Declared Safe
Why the St. Francis Dam Collapsed
The Inspection, Then the Flood
soru: Would you have called it safe?
sahneler: Just before midnight, a California dam burst.
A wall of water swept down the valley toward the sea, killing hundreds.
That same morning, it had been inspected and called safe.
The engineers had seen new leaks.
They looked like the usual seepage.
But the rock beneath one side was weak and softening.
When it gave way, the dam broke apart.
California then created state oversight for dam safety.

kaynakca.ad: ASDSO Dam Failures and Lessons Learned — St. Francis Dam (California, 1928)

baslik: The Bridge That Collapsed Under Its Own Weight
sonuc: collapsed into the St. Lawrence River during construction
tetik: a weight estimate that was never recalculated after the span grew
mekanizma: buckling of an overloaded lower compression chord
ders: the collapse is remembered in the Iron Ring ceremony for Canadian engineers

zaman.olay: South cantilever collapses during construction

yanilgi: The collapse wasn't sudden and unannounced. Workers had measured a steel chord bending more each day.
tartisma: An engineer ordered work stopped, but the message arrived too late. How fast should a warning travel?
basliklar: The Bridge That Collapsed Under Its Own Weight
Why the Quebec Bridge Fell
The Warning That Came Too Late
sahneler: A giant bridge collapsed into the St. Lawrence River while it was being built.
Seventy five workers were killed.
It was crushed by its own weight.
The span had been lengthened during design.
But the weight of the steel was never properly recalculated.
Workers saw a key steel chord bending more each day.
The order to stop came too late.
Canadian engineers still recall it in the Iron Ring ceremony.

kaynakca.ad: The Canadian Encyclopedia — Quebec Bridge Disasters

baslik: A Ship Full of Fertilizer Exploded in a Harbor
sonuc: exploded in the port of Texas City
tetik: a fire in a hold full of ammonium nitrate
mekanizma: detonation of ammonium nitrate fertilizer heated in a closed, steam-smothered hold
ders: ammonium nitrate handling and port storage rules were tightened
zincir: FIRES SET OFF A SECOND SHIP

zaman.olay: Grandcamp explodes; High Flyer explodes the next day

yanilgi: Pumping in steam didn't smother the fire. It helped heat the ammonium nitrate toward detonation.
tartisma: Crowds gathered to watch the burning ship. How close is too close to a fire you don't understand?
basliklar: A Ship Full of Fertilizer Exploded in a Harbor
Why the Texas City Disaster Happened
The Fire They Tried to Smother With Steam
sahneler: A cargo ship exploded in a Texas harbor.
The blast flattened the waterfront and killed hundreds.
Its cargo was ammonium nitrate fertilizer.
A fire had started deep in the hold.
The crew closed the hatches and pumped in steam to smother it.
That trapped heat, and the fertilizer detonated.
The next day, a second ship exploded too.
Rules for storing and shipping ammonium nitrate were tightened.

kaynakca.ad: Texas State Historical Association — Texas City Disaster

baslik: The Backup Generators Were in the Basement
sonuc: suffered three reactor meltdowns
tetik: a tsunami flooding the backup power systems
mekanizma: station blackout from flooded emergency diesel generators and switchgear, causing loss of cooling
ders: plants worldwide added flood protection and portable backup power

zaman.olay: Earthquake and tsunami; station blackout

yanilgi: The earthquake didn't cause the meltdowns. The reactors shut down safely; it was the tsunami's flooding of backup power that stopped the cooling.
tartisma: Studies had warned of taller tsunamis. How rare does a threat have to be before you ignore it?
basliklar: The Backup Generators Were in the Basement
Why Fukushima Melted Down
The Tsunami That Killed the Cooling
soru: Where would you put the generators?
sahneler: Three nuclear reactors at Fukushima melted down.
Within days, hydrogen explosions destroyed reactor buildings.
The earthquake didn't do it.
The reactors had already shut down safely.
Then a tsunami poured over the seawall.
It flooded the backup generators and electrical rooms.
Without power, the cooling pumps stopped.
Plants worldwide then added flood protection and mobile backup power.

kaynakca.ad: IAEA — The Fukushima Daiichi Accident, Report by the Director General

baslik: Titanic Could Survive Four Flooded Compartments — Not More
sonuc: sank on her maiden voyage
tetik: an iceberg scraping along the starboard side
mekanizma: hull breaches across more watertight compartments than the design could survive
ders: SOLAS rules made lifeboats for everyone aboard mandatory

zaman.olay: Collision late on April 14; sinks early April 15

yanilgi: Titanic's bulkheads were not open-topped by accident, but they didn't reach high enough. As the bow sank, water spilled over them one by one.
tartisma: Titanic carried more lifeboats than the law required. How can a ship meet the rules and still fail?
basliklar: Titanic Could Survive Four Flooded Compartments — Not More
Why the Titanic Sank So Fast
The Watertight Walls That Weren't High Enough
sahneler: Titanic sank on her maiden voyage.
It went down in two hours and forty minutes, and more than fifteen hundred people died.
It was built to stay afloat with four compartments flooded.
The iceberg opened more than that along the side.
As the bow sank lower, water spilled over the watertight walls.
They weren't high enough to stop it.
There weren't enough lifeboats for everyone.
Now international rules require lifeboats for everyone aboard.

kaynakca.ad: IMO — International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS), 1974
